title: Settings restore crashes and leaves settings unusable

judgment.rationale: The report and diagnostic analysis identify malformed JSON across several module settings during restore. RestoreSettings parses, normalizes, compares, and merges module files under an outer generic catch; this is a concrete robustness gap, although the exact malformed input and desired recovery policy are not yet pinned down.
judgment.recommended_action: Define per-file validation and a non-destructive restore policy for malformed module settings, then test mixed valid/invalid backups.

evidence.fact: Automated diagnostic analysis reported malformed JSON in several module settings during restoration and the author reports a crash/unusable settings window.
SettingsBackupAndRestoreUtils.RestoreSettings enumerates backup files, parses export metadata, compares normalized JSON, and merges or overwrites settings under a broad outer error path.
No public fix PR was identified for the reported restore failure.

fix_assessment.rationale: The malformed-input handling boundary is identifiable, but the recovery policy and exact offending files need confirmation before implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Make settings restore resilient to malformed module JSON
proposed_fixes.root_cause: RestoreSettings can abort while parsing or merging malformed module files, and its broad catch does not establish a safe transactional outcome.
plan: Validate backup metadata and each module JSON before applying any changes.
Apply the agreed skip-and-report or all-or-nothing policy without partially overwriting settings.
Surface a public-safe module-level failure summary and preserve the original settings on fatal restore failure.
verification: A backup containing one malformed module does not crash Settings.
Valid modules restore and invalid modules are reported according to the chosen policy.
A failed restore leaves a byte-equivalent or semantically equivalent pre-restore configuration.

confidence.rationale: The code boundary and failure class are concrete, but the intended recovery policy remains open.

issue_context.summary: Restoring a settings backup can crash and leave the Settings experience unusable when module JSON is malformed.
known_information: The issue includes a diagnostic report and automated analysis.
The restore implementation parses and merges module JSON and returns a generic backup error from its outer catch.
The failure spans multiple module settings according to the diagnostic analysis.
inferences: A single malformed file may abort an otherwise recoverable restore.
The user may need per-file reporting and preservation of the pre-restore settings state.
issue_context.analysis: Audit every parse/merge boundary and make restore transactional at the file or backup level.

information_gaps.information: The backup version, exact malformed module files, and whether the expected behavior is skip-and-report or reject-and-rollback.
information_gaps.why_needed: Those details determine the safe recovery contract and prevent silently dropping user settings.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce with a copy of the backup, run /bugreport after the failure, and identify the affected module names without sharing private setting values.

actions.label: Request targeted evidence
actions.note: Pin down the restore recovery contract and offending file set.

comment.body: The diagnostic analysis already points to malformed JSON in multiple module settings, so a generic request for more logs would not help. Please identify the backup/export version and the module names that fail, and confirm whether the desired behavior is to skip invalid module files while restoring valid ones or to reject the entire backup and leave existing settings untouched. Reproduce once and run /bugreport immediately after the Settings window becomes unusable; do not include private setting values.

actions.label: Approve focused fix design
actions.note: The proposed design is specific enough for fork-side implementation after maintainer approval.

design.scope: Make settings restore validate each module file before merge and preserve a recoverable pre-restore state.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed module JSON produces a clear per-file error without crashing Settings.
Valid module settings are restored according to the agreed skip-or-rollback policy.
A failed restore leaves the previous settings intact and the Settings UI usable.
